Congratulations are in order for a physicist whose lab has spent decades making clocks so precise that they wouldn’t lose a second in the age of the universe. This week, she was awarded one of the field’s most prestigious international prizes for her contributions to atomic physics. Colleagues describe her as relentless, curious, and a little bit stubborn — in the best way. Her group’s work has helped redefine how scientists measure time, and it’s opening doors to tests of fundamental physics that once seemed impossible. Asked what she’s most proud of, she laughed and said it’s her students. “They’re the ones who’ll take this further than I ever could,” she said. The prize will be presented at a ceremony next spring.
